newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sacks sports chief amid talk of infighting.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sacks sports chief amid talk of infighting.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Monday formally removed his one-time confidant as Russia's sports chief, heightening talk of new infighting in his entourage.
The presidential press service said in a brief statement that Yeltsin had issued a decree removing Shamil Tarpishchev as chairman of the State Committee on Sports and Tourism from November 1.
It gave no explanation for the delay but said Tarpishchev was being moved to other work.

A former tennis professional, he rose to power through his friendship with Yeltsin, who was his tennis pupil, and Alexander Korzhakov, who was sacked as head of the president's personal security in June.
Confirmation of Tarpishchev's dismissal, reported by partly government-owned ORT television on Saturday, followed a rash of corruption charges by former Yeltsin aides and officials.
Boris Fyodorov, former head of the National Sports Fund, accused Korzhakov of trying to extort $40 million from the Fund.

The timing of the charge, made in separate TV interviews on Sunday and Monday, suggested an attempt to block any alliance between Korzhakov and the ambitious General Alexander Lebed, who has his sights set on succeeding Yeltsin as president.
Fyodorov narrowly escaped an attempt to kill him in June and walks with a stick after being shot and stabbed outside his ostensibly well-guarded official residence.
Korzhakov, who blames Yeltsin's daughter and the new Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais for his sacking, could not be reached for comment. He is not charged with any offence.
The Sports Fund, described by Russian newspapers as an all-purpose Kremlin slush fund, used a lucrative tax break to import alcohol and tobacco free of duty, making huge profits.
The money was supposed to go into developing Russian sport, but some sports administrators have complained that they have seen little cash.
NTV commercial television linked Fyodorov's accusation against Korzhakov with Lebed's need for political funding.

The former paratroop general, now Yeltsin's national security adviser, entered politics just a year ago but has open presidential ambitions and has irritated Kremlin insiders by grabbing headlines and openly criticising the government of Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
"On one side, Lebed has clear problems financing his political activity," NTV presenter Yevgeny Kiselyov said.
"On the other side, there is Korzhakov, who until very recently controlled, through his people, two very rich organisations...the National Sports Fund and (arms export agency) Rosvooruzhenye."
Korzhakov said last month Lebed would be the next president. The burly former bodyguard wants to run for parliament, possibly for the Tula seat Lebed had to resign after joining the Kremlin.
Lebed has spoken up in defence of Korzhakov.

In a direct attack on Lebed on Monday, Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov, whom Lebed demanded should be sacked last August, repeated his attacks on the peace deal Lebed reached in Chechnya. Lebed was in Brussels, visiting NATO headquarters.
